sections.content: You know *si* + imperfect subjunctive (B1 Unit 7), the conditional (A2 Unit 26) and *quizá* (B1 Unit 25). Here you combine them to imagine possible futures: a *si* clause plus *quizá*, *probablemente*, *podría*, *sería* or *tendría*. The marker shows how uncertain the scenario is.

items.spanish: Si viviéramos en otro lugar, quizá tendríamos una vida diferente.
items.english: If we lived somewhere else, perhaps we would have a different life.

items.spanish: En ese escenario, podría ocurrir algo inesperado.
items.english: In that scenario, something unexpected could happen.

items.spanish: Sería difícil saber qué resultado tendríamos.
items.english: It would be difficult to know what outcome we would have.

items.spanish: Si cambiara la situación, probablemente cambiarían nuestras decisiones.
items.english: If the situation changed, our decisions would probably change.

sections.content: You know the simple future from A2 Unit 19 and the past participle from A2 Unit 1. The *futuro perfecto* combines them: *haber* in the future (*habré, habrás, habrá, habremos, habréis, habrán*) + the participle, which does not change. It says that something will already be finished by a point in the future: *En 2030 habremos terminado la casa.* Spanish also uses it to guess about the past: *Habrá salido ya* means "he has probably left already". This lesson practises only the first use.

sections.title: Futuro perfecto: haber + participle
rows: he, she, you (formal) will have finished
they, you all will have finished

items.english: By 2030 we will have finished the house.

items.spanish: Para el viernes habré terminado el trabajo.
items.english: By Friday I will have finished the work.

items.spanish: Dentro de diez años, la situación habrá cambiado mucho.
items.english: In ten years, the situation will have changed a lot.

items.spanish: No contesta el teléfono; habrá salido ya.
items.english: He is not answering the phone; he has probably left already.

sections.content: A hypothetical answer can contain both a condition and a probability marker to show degrees of uncertainty.
